title: Clock gene signature predicts insomnia and links to sleep/circadian parameters.
authors: Carvalhas-Almeida, Catarina; Alves, Joao; Davi, Tiago; Santos, Barbara; Gaspar, Laetitia; Ribeiro, Rodrigo F N; Serra, Joana; Ferreira, Mafalda; Moita, Joaquim; Sehgal, Amita; Cavadas, Claudia; Alvaro, Ana Rita
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用机器学习分析时钟基因表达预测失眠，但对象为基因表达与睡眠表型关联，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点或结构建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Chronic Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder that remains difficult to diagnose due to subjective symptoms and heterogeneous presentations. The most severe form, insomnia with short sleep duration (ISSD), is defined by a total sleep time of less than six hours on polysomnography. However, objective assessments are rarely recommended in diagnostic guidelines, highlighting the need for alternative biomarkers. Disruptions in the circadian clock system may contribute to chronic insomnia, though the extent of these effects remains unclear. In this study, we investigate sleep and circadian rhythm-related alterations in chronic insomnia and its subtypes, ISSD and insomnia with normal sleep duration (INSD), by assessing plasma cortisol, wrist and axillary temperature, and clock gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Additionally, we use machine learning to identify the most relevant clock genes for detecting insomnia and classifying its subtypes. Chronic insomnia patients exhibited reduced body temperature rhythms, elevated cortisol levels during wake before sleep, and significant alterations in clock gene expression, including in BMAL1, PER1-2, REV-ERBalpha, and REV-ERBbeta, compared to controls. Most alterations were more significant in the ISSD group. Moreover, associations between clock gene expression, sleep-related parameters and Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores were identified. Using machine learning, we identified three genes as sensitive biomarkers distinguishing chronic insomnia from controls and differentiating between ISSD and INSD subtypes. Our findings suggest that circadian markers and machine learning could improve understanding of chronic insomnia and aid biomarker discovery for diagnosis.
abstract_zh: 慢性失眠是一种常见的睡眠障碍，由于其主观症状和异质性表现，诊断仍然困难。其最严重形式，即短睡眠时长失眠（ISSD），通过多导睡眠图定义总睡眠时间少于六小时。然而，客观评估在诊断指南中很少被推荐，这凸显了对替代生物标志物的需求。昼夜节律系统的紊乱可能促成慢性失眠，但这些影响的程度仍不清楚。在本研究中，我们通过评估血浆皮质醇、腕部和腋窝温度以及外周血单核细胞（PBMCs）中的时钟基因表达，探讨慢性失眠及其亚型ISSD和正常睡眠时长失眠（INSD）中与睡眠和昼夜节律相关的改变。此外，我们使用机器学习来识别最相关的时钟基因，用于检测失眠及其亚型分类。与对照组相比，慢性失眠患者表现出体温节律降低、睡眠前清醒期间皮质醇水平升高，以及时钟基因表达的显著改变，包括BMAL1、PER1-2、REV-ERBalpha和REV-ERBbeta。大多数改变在ISSD组中更为显著。此外，我们识别出时钟基因表达、睡眠相关参数和失眠严重程度指数（ISI）评分之间的关联。通过机器学习，我们确定了三个基因作为敏感生物标志物，用于区分慢性失眠与对照组，并区分ISSD和INSD亚型。我们的发现表明，昼夜节律标志物和机器学习可能增进对慢性失眠的理解，并有助于诊断的生物标志物发现。
